title: Carina: waist, head and trouser fixes
by: Claude, recovered and checked by Codex
question: Selected: carina-2-r2-grey.

media.caption: First diagnostic render: the original waist from four angles.
First seam repair render, retained in order.
Closer diagnostic render before the final comparison sheets.

Round 2, your words on carina-2: "she has a small seam at the waist. Her head should be 15% smaller. Her pants should be a different color". 1, the seam. It was in the texture, not the mesh or the rig: the underside of her top's hem and the top edge of the trousers were painted beige by Meshy's texture pass, which showed as a dotted light line under the hem. Painted out in Blender with the top's and the trousers' own colour on just those faces. Close-ups at the waist, before and after; these trousers are still black so only the seam changes, and the last one is the earlier version with denim.

2, the head 15% smaller. Hair and face scaled to 0.85 about the top of her neck in Blender, with the body unchanged, so the rig, the joints and the skin weights come out the same. The game stands every model at its own height, so she is still 1.12 tall, with a smaller head on a slightly bigger body. Front and side, before and after, both at 1.12.
The head close up after the change: face, eyes and hair are only scaled, nothing repainted. Before and after from the front and at three-quarter, then the other three-quarter and the back.

3, the trousers. You didn't name a colour, so the first refinement used dark denim blue: it stands out against her black top and differs from her black top. Mid-grey was selected on 2026-10-06 and is now installed. Only the trousers part of the texture is changed, done in Blender. Each spot keeps its own light and dark, so the shading and folds stay as they were. Her shoes are separate and didn't change.
All three together, three-quarter view: before, after with denim (earlier), after with grey, and the back with denim.
Earlier fitted-rig diagnostic: walk frames 1 to 26 retained in sequence. Its backward knee bending was found in the full-cycle joint check, so the native rig below replaces it.
Her head in the walk, front and side: it turns and nods with the head joint as before (100% on the head bone), and no part of the neck or collar shows through the smaller head.

Native rig diagnostic: the same edited model with Meshy's native skeleton, repaired weights and walk/run/sit clips. The earlier fitted rig bent the knees backward during part of the walk; this one keeps forward knee flexion across the cycle. The sit clip cost 3 Meshy credits before recovery; no credits spent during recovery.
